Unit positions come from the Revolutionary War workbook (the Cowpens rows), built from Morgan's report, Tarleton's and Howard's accounts, the journals and memoirs of men in the ranks, the Army's 1996 staff ride handbook, the Army War College study of 1928 and the National Park Service's handbook and waysides. Nothing here has been checked by a historian.

No map made at the time shows this ground, and the accounts give distances, not places. Every unit is therefore placed by distance along the Green River Road, which still crosses the field, counted from the spot where Tarleton's column came out of the woods. Lines may be 50 to 100 m from where they really stood; none is rated better than medium.

The clock follows the staff ride's maps: first shots about 07:00, the end about 07:50. Eyewitnesses say only "about sunrise", which was at 07:07; one Army study puts everything an hour later. Tap a unit to see the range of times its record allows.
Solid symbols are positions a source gives. Dashed symbols are worked out or are the last position on record. A question mark means the place is doubtful.
Symbols are blue for the Americans and red for the British and Loyalist troops. Zoom in to see Pickens's line by its regiments and Howard's by its parts.

The current map is the US Geological Survey's topographic map, and Satellite its aerial photography, both streamed from the USGS. If they cannot be reached, a simplified drawing of OpenStreetMap roads and streams is shown instead.

Where the sources disagree (the hour, the numbers, which riflemen were on the right, how far Howard fell back, who brought the militia back), the workbook's Hypotheses sheet gives each reading and says which one the playback follows.

The playback opens on "1781 with terrain", a reconstruction: the roads Edwin Bearss drew in 1967 as the roads of the battle, laid on the ground by the road the park still keeps, and today's ground, which the park has kept open. The map details (the i button) list each road with its source and how sure it is, and offer the other maps of this ground: Bearss's own maps phase by phase, the Army War College sketches of 1928, the USGS maps of 1959 and 1975, Mills's map of 1825 and the park map.
